pairs.question: Age, si quis vellet ea facultate bonus fieri, qua boni sunt coqui, qui sciti in primis habentur, unde fieret?
pairs.answer: Inde videlicet, si de bonis coquis disceret.
pairs.derivation: Socrates asks where one would become good in the cookery skill; Amicus answers directly. Whole interrogative kept contiguous; answer is the complete reply.

pairs.question: Quid, si vellet bonus fieri medicus, ad quem profectus, bonus fieret medicus?
pairs.answer: Ad eorum aliquem, qui boni sunt medici.
pairs.derivation: Socrates asks to whom one would go to become a good doctor; Amicus answers. Complete question and complete reply, no trimming needed.

pairs.question: Estne igitur aliquis, qui laedi malit quam iuvari?
pairs.derivation: Genuine interrogative (Estne... -ne) answered directly by Amicus. Complete reply kept.

pairs.question: Quo igitur pacto, Socrates, boni tibi fieri videntur? Si enim natura, neque disciplina fiunt, quonam tandem alio modo fiant boni?
pairs.answer: Reor equidem hoc ipsum non ita facile posse declarari: siquidem suspicor huiusce rei possessionem quiddam maxime divinum esse, et si bonos fieri similiter, atque divini vates et fatidici fiunt, sed spiritu, quo divinitus afflantur.
pairs.derivation: Amicus's entire speech is one question (kept verbatim and contiguous). Socrates's reply is trimmed to the operative answering sentence (ending at the first full stop after 'afflantur'); what follows ('Sic et viri boni...') elaborates and digresses, so it is cut.
